requirements:
Build a deterministic directed graph analyzer.

R1. Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with `rustc --edition 2024`, std only. Do not use inner attributes (`#![...]`) or inner documentation (`//!`). Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences.

R2. Expose exactly the following public API (field types, variant fields and derives are part of the contract). Function bodies and private helpers/state are yours to implement:
```rust
pub const MAX_VERTICES: usize = 4096;
pub const MAX_EDGES: usize = 32768;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GraphError {
    TooManyVertices { count: usize, limit: usize },
    TooManyEdges { limit: usize },
    BadEndpoint { edge: usize, side: u8, vertex: usize },
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Graph {
    pub components: Vec<Vec<usize>>,
    pub component_of: Vec<usize>,
    pub cyclic: Vec<bool>,
}
pub fn analyze(n: usize, edges: &[(usize, usize)]) -> Result<Graph, GraphError>;
```

R3. `analyze(n, edges)` analyzes vertices numbered 0 through n-1. Every tuple is a directed edge (source, target). All outputs are owned values. There is no persistent state in analyze.

R4. Validate before analyzing. First, if n > MAX_VERTICES return TooManyVertices { count: n, limit: MAX_VERTICES }, even if the edge list is too long or invalid. n = MAX_VERTICES is allowed.

R5. Next, if edges.len() > MAX_EDGES return TooManyEdges { limit: MAX_EDGES }, before inspecting endpoints. Exactly MAX_EDGES edges is allowed.

R6. Next scan input edges in their original order. Return BadEndpoint for the first edge with an endpoint >= n; edge is its zero-based input index. Check source (side: 0) before target (side: 1) within that edge. vertex is the offending value, unmodified.

R7. All endpoint errors use the position in the original slice, including preceding duplicate edges, internal edges and self-loops; do not deduplicate before validating. Values as large as usize::MAX are ordinary invalid endpoints, not special sentinels.

R8. Reachability means a directed path, allowing a zero-length path from a vertex to itself.

R9. The components partition all vertices into maximal sets of mutually reachable vertices; isolated vertices appear too. Edges are directed, not undirected.

R10. Each component is a nonempty vector of its distinct vertex numbers sorted ascending.

R11. Sort components by DECREASING number of vertices, then INCREASING smallest member on equal sizes. A component ID is its zero-based index in this sorted vector, not its minimum vertex or traversal number.

R12. component_of has length n; component_of[v] is the canonical component ID of v.

R13. cyclic has one entry per component: true exactly when that component has at least two vertices OR it contains a self-loop edge. A singleton without a self-loop has false, even if it has incoming or outgoing edges.

R14. Duplicate edges and self-loops are legal and count toward the edge limit. Duplicates do not change SCC membership or cyclic flags.

R15. For n = 0 the empty edge list succeeds with all Graph vector fields empty; any nonempty edge list within the edge limit fails at its first source endpoint.

R16. For n > 0 with no edges the components are [0], [1], ..., [n-1], component_of[v] = v, and every cyclic flag is false.

R17. For a valid graph, permuting the input edges cannot change components, component_of or cyclic. Any fields expressly defined by input position in later clauses may change.

R18. All inputs within the stated limits must be supported, including disconnected graphs, long directed paths, and a component containing all vertices. Valid calls return normally without panics. No particular SCC algorithm is required.
